lines.text: Spring mud warning! Roads shut. Tractors stuck. Cows confused.
Mud season! My cousin's got an MX track out behind the soybeans!
Dirt bikes? Aren't those just mopeds that hate you?
Yep. Build a dirt bike. Two-strokes scream, four-strokes pull.
And premix the two-strokes. 32 to 1. If you eyeball it, I'll eyeball you.
The Creekbed Hare Scramble is this month. Bring boots. Bring two pairs.
I rebuilt Grandpa's tractor carb at nine. This is just smaller. And angrier.
Round-slide carb, needle clip, main jet. Clip down richens the midrange.
It's loud. I love it. Can I keep it?
Rosie came back so muddy her mom rented her out as a scarecrow!
Worth it. I got dirt in places dirt shouldn't know about.
Mud on their faces, trophy in their hands. That's Tinplate, folks.
My cousin says we can use the track anytime. The cows like Rosie.
You've got a dirt program now, kid. Augie would've loved it. He hated mud.
Hon, terrible news. Crownwell Holdings bought Corn Belt Oil this morning.
They voided every racing contract that isn't Crownwell. I'm so sorry.
I did make them pay the exit fee. In full. In cash. Here.
Can't beat us on track, so she buys the oil. Classic Crownwell.
Well. Friday night, drag strip. That's where I got my name. Come on.
1977. County Line Quarter. I won it on jetting alone. Hence: Jets.
So: win a drag race, research race fuel and find a new sponsor.
Lights on the tree! Yellow, yellow, yellow, GREEN! And they're gone, folks!
Launch is everything. Good reaction, clean shift, and pray for traction.
A new sponsor! Good. Now guess who got a new job? This gal!
Hot Dog Hut, regional marketing! Snappy dogs, snappy laps!
Friday Night Drags belong to Tinplate! Hazel 'Jets' Pruitt is grinning. Rare!
Don't get used to it.
And Crownwell can keep their oil. We've got hot dogs!
Race weekend forecast: rain. Then more rain. Then a surprise. Also rain.
Wet track: smooth hands, early brakes, stay off the painted lines.
Rain tires, softer setup. Cool damp air is dense, so richen it a hair.
Smooth hands? I don't own smooth hands.
Then borrow mine. Win a wet race and I'll buy the pizza.
Rainy Day Derby and the Monsoon Mile are on the calendar. Bring towels.
Boss... Preston's in the ditch on the back straight. His crew left him.
We could tow him out with the pickup. Or let him swim.

reply.text: Kidding. I already hooked the chain. He says thanks. Kinda.

lines.text: A Tinplate pickup towing a Crownwell car! Somebody get the Clarion a photo!
That was a wet win, kid. Smooth as gravy. I owe somebody a pizza.
Extra cheese. Extra everything. Extra-extra.
I, uh, left a fruit basket at your door. It's from me. Not Mother.
Hillclimb season! One machine, one mountain, one clock. And thin air.
Every thousand meters up, the air thins. Same jets, less air. Runs rich.
So jet DOWN going up. Carbs don't adjust themselves. EFI wants a baro sensor.
She's right. Midge Ostrowski, chief engineer, Crownwell. Twenty-two years.
Off the record? Your jetting at altitude last month beat ours.
...I like her. I don't want to. But I do.
Preston wrecked on the climb. He ignored my call and Victoria blamed me.
Twenty-two years, and I'm why her boy can't brake. I'm done.
Your team listens to its mechanics. Is there room for one more?

reply.text: Ha! I brought my own torque wrench. Show me where the coffee is.
Don't trust me. Trust my torque wrench. It's never lied to anybody.

lines.text: A real chief engineer! Can I ask you about cam timing? Like, all of it?
Finish the hill program first. Then I'm yours. Then the cams are yours.
King of the Hill: Tinplate! And a defection! Midge Ostrowski switches teams!
Midge. After twenty-two years. You will regret this.
I regret the twenty-two years, Victoria. Not this.
Augie raced both. Said a bike teaches you what a car forgives.
So a car title AND a bike title? I'll need more garage. And sleep.
Two programs, one crew. Crownwell never managed it. Too many egos.
Folks, nobody's won titles on two wheels and four in the same era. Nobody!
That's one! Hey Dewey, which one's next, wheels-wise?
The other number of wheels.
Two wheels AND four! Tinplate does what Crownwell never could!
Augie, you old goat. They did it. Both ways.
One World title's nice. Two opens the Legend tier. Ask anybody. Ask me!
Hon, Hot Dog Hut is going international! Snappy dogs, worldwide laps!
Two titles. Ambitious. Crownwell holds four. My father held nine.
Her father beat Augie in the '79 Cup. Bent a rule, broke a heart.
Mother's furious you're winning. I've never seen her this... awake.
I've been tuning my own car at night. Midge left notes. Don't tell anyone.
Two World titles! The Legend tier is OPEN! I'm out of exclamation points!
Legend tier. Volcanoes. Sky highways. Glacier planets. Don't ask, just race.
Found something in Augie's footlocker. His notebook. 1979.
The Crownwell Cup. Augie against Victoria's father. Augie lost by a nose.
Bent wastegate rule. Everybody knew. Nobody said. Augie never raced again.
The last page says: 'Somebody finish this.' That's you, kid.
Then we build. Get a machine to Lv 8 and win at Legend level.
A Legend win. You're at my level now. Don't stop.
The Ultimate Crown. She's booked it for the Cup. I'll be there.
King of All Terrain. Final round, the Ultimate Crown. That is the Cup.
My father beat Augie Moss there. I intend to keep it in the family.
Not this time, Victoria.
